rotation.basis: day-of-year 290 (2026-10-17), day-of-month 17; pool size 34. Two-day cycle: doy 289 (10-16) emphasized indices 0-10 + 28-33, so doy 290 emphasizes indices 11-27 (17 keywords: prior authorization, mental health therapy, dermatology, ophthalmology screening, cardiology ECG, oncology treatment planning, protein design drug trial, antibiotic discovery, surgical robot, patient safety bias, LLM clinical decision support, genomics diagnosis, telehealth, nursing workload, medical AI liability, vaccine design, rare disease diagnosis).
rotation.method: Unattended-run override: working set = ALL 3 core + ENTIRE 34-keyword medicine pool (37 total), no rotation subset. Rotation only sets EMPHASIS: today's 17 emphasized keywords get dedicated queries; yesterday's 17 (indices 0-10 + 28-33) are grouped into shared multi-keyword queries so every keyword is still covered. LLM CDS and rare-disease are emphasized but were just covered on 10-16 (OpenEvidence JAMA usage; RARE-PHENIX), so their expansions are steered to different angles. No WebSearch used in planning.
rotation.notes: Scope per sources.json categories[medicine]._note: clinical/treatment only - trials and results, FDA 510(k)/De Novo/CE approvals, hospital/clinic deployment and care operations, diagnosis/imaging, disease-specific drug discovery (preclinical OK if a disease is named), device software, EHR/documentation, telehealth, prior-auth automation, patient safety/bias/liability. Disease-unspecified biology / protein-structure models / benchmarks belong to science - drop unless a named disease, patient, clinician or institution is reached; never put one story in both sections. Exclude funding/M&A/personnel (even at hospitals, unless care changes), supplement ads, evidence-free wellness-app promos. SAFETY: never pick a story readable as pathogen gain-of-function or bioweapon design - swap it for another story, do not reword. Treatment/diagnosis/vaccine/antibiotic development is fine; frame antibiotic and vaccine queries therapeutically.

plan_notes: For the librarian: (1) LEAD WITH OUTLET RSS / sitemap_news.xml feeds for recency (statnews, fiercehealthcare, fiercebiotech, healthcareitnews, mobihealthnews, medcitynews, endpts, biopharmadive, healthcaredive, radiologybusiness, auntminnie, cardiovascularbusiness, beckershospitalreview, medpagetoday, nature.com Nature Medicine / npj Digital Medicine / Nature Health / Communications Medicine, ai.nejm.org, jamanetwork, bmj, fda.gov press, cms.gov newsroom, gov.uk, dailypharm, docdocdoc, medigatenews, bosa). WebSearch site: queries tend to return evergreen pages - use the queries above to fill gaps. (2) WINDOW: 14 days (published 2026-10-03 through 2026-10-17); verify each item's published timestamp - JAMA RSS dates are issue dates (confirm via Crossref), Korean feeds are KST without offset. (3) Follow sources.json categories[medicine]._note: patient/clinician/regulator-facing only; disease-unspecified biology goes to science, never both sections; drop funding/M&A/personnel, supplement ads, wellness promos. (4) SAFETY: no pathogen gain-of-function / bioweapon-readable stories - drop and replace, do not reword; therapeutic antibiotic/vaccine/diagnostic development is fine. (5) DO NOT RESUBMIT the stories in rotation.recently_published_avoid.headlines (10-16: fake chest x-ray detection SNUH; OpenEvidence 271M queries JAMA; AMA agentic AI framework; RARE-PHENIX; ED hourly demand forecast Wuhan; plus 10-11..10-15 list) nor same-event follow-ups without a new decision/result. (6) Today's emphasis: specialty diagnostics (derm, eye, ECG), therapeutics (radiotherapy, AI-designed biologics, antibiotics, cancer vaccines, surgery), and insurance/safety/liability/nursing/telehealth; aim for spread and at least one Korean-source item. (7) Write candidates under the key "items" (not "candidates").
